def: The smallest number of single-character edits needed to turn one string into another.
A spelling model that picks the word maximising its prior probability times the probability of the observed typo.
Adding related terms, such as synonyms, to a query so that documents using different words can match.
The loss of the original meaning when added or relaxed query terms pull results away from what the user wanted.
Treating the top results of a first search as relevant and adding their characteristic terms to a second search.
Retrying a query that returned too few results with fewer required terms.
Broder's three intents: reaching a known page, seeking information, and wanting to do something.
The very frequent, middling and very rare parts of the distribution of queries in a log.
The pattern in which the frequency of the r-th most common item is roughly proportional to 1/r.
